nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M \times M \to M$ is measurable. For all s-finite measures $a, b, c, d$ on $M$ we have $(a * b) * (c * d) = (a * c) * (b * d)$, where $*$ denotes convolution of measures.
nodes.title: Interchange law for convolution

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M 	imes M 	o M$ is measurable, and let $
u$ be an s-finite measure on $M$. Writing $*$ for convolution of measures and $
u^{*n}$ for the $n$-th convolution power of $
u$, for all natural numbers $m$ and $n$ we have $
u^{*(m+n)} = 
u^{*m} * 
u^{*n}$.
nodes.title: Convolution powers add exponents

Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M 	imes M 	o M$ is measurable, and let $
u$ and $ho$ be s-finite measures on $M$. Writing $*$ for convolution of measures and $\mu^{*n}$ for the $n$-th convolution power of a measure $\mu$, for every natural number $n$ we have $(

nodes.title: Convolution power of a convolution

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M \times M \to M$ is measurable. For every point $x \in M$ and every natural number $n$, the $n$-th convolution power of the Dirac measure $\delta_x$ is $\delta_{nx}$, where $nx$ is the sum of $n$ copies of $x$ (so $0x = 0$).
nodes.title: Convolution powers of a Dirac measure

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M 	imes M 	o M$ is measurable, and let $
u$ be an s-finite measure on $M$. Then the first convolution power of $
u$ is $
u$ itself.
nodes.title: The first convolution power

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra for which addition $M 	imes M 	o M$ is measurable, and let $
u$ be an s-finite measure on $M$. For every natural number $n$, the $(n+1)$-st convolution power of $
u$ equals the measure obtained from $
u$ by applying the map $\mu \mapsto 
u * \mu$ exactly $n$ times, where $*$ denotes convolution of measures.
nodes.title: Convolution powers as iterated left convolution

nodes.summary: For every real rate $r \ge 0$ and every natural number $n$, the $(n+1)$-st convolution power of the Poisson measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with rate $r$ is the Poisson measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with rate $(n+1)r$.
nodes.title: Convolution powers of a Poisson measure

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra and let $
u$ be a measure on $M$. For every natural number $n$, the $(n+1)$-st convolution power of $
u$ is the convolution of the $n$-th convolution power of $
u$ with $
u$.
nodes.title: Recursion for convolution powers

nodes.summary: For every measure $\nu$ on an additive commutative monoid $M$ with a σ-algebra, the zeroth convolution power of $\nu$ is the Dirac measure $\delta_0$ at the identity element $0$ of $M$.
nodes.title: The zeroth convolution power

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a σ-algebra and let $
u$ be a measure on $M$. The $n$-th convolution power $
u^{*n}$ of $
u$ is defined by recursion on $n$: $
u^{*0} = \delta_0$, the Dirac measure at the identity $0$ of $M$, and $
u^{*(n+1)} = 
u^{*n} * 
u$, where $*$ denotes convolution of measures.
nodes.title: Convolution power of a measure

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a measurable structure in which addition is jointly measurable. If $\mu$ and $\eta$ are infinitely divisible measures on $M$, then their convolution $\mu * \eta$ is infinitely divisible.
nodes.title: Infinite divisibility is closed under convolution

nodes.summary: For every real number $a$, the Dirac measure $\delta_a$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is infinitely divisible: for every $n \ge 1$, $\delta_a$ is the $n$-fold convolution power of $\delta_{a/n}$.
nodes.title: Dirac measures on the real line are infinitely divisible

nodes.summary: For every real $r \ge 0$, the Poisson distribution with parameter $r$, as a measure on $\mathbb{N}$, is infinitely divisible: for every $n \ge 1$ it is the $n$-fold convolution power of the Poisson distribution with parameter $r/n$.
nodes.title: Poisson distributions are infinitely divisible

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a measurable structure in which addition is jointly measurable. A measure $\mu$ on $M$ is infinitely divisible if for every natural number $n \ge 1$ there is a probability measure $\nu$ on $M$ whose $n$-fold convolution power $\nu^{*n}$ equals $\mu$.
nodes.title: Infinitely divisible measures

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a measurable structure. If $\nu$ is a probability measure on $M$, then for every natural number $n$ its $n$-fold convolution power $\nu^{*n}$ is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Convolution powers of a probability measure are probability measures

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a measurable structure in which addition is jointly measurable. Every infinitely divisible measure on $M$ is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Infinitely divisible measures are probability measures

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid with a measurable structure. If $\nu$ is an s-finite measure on $M$, then for every natural number $n$ its $n$-fold convolution power $\nu^{*n}$ is s-finite.
nodes.title: Convolution powers of an s-finite measure are s-finite

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
